name: Blemish
overview: Scripture, particularly in Leviticus 21:17-22, teaches that any physical blemish disqualifies a son of Aaron from performing priestly duties, emphasizing the necessity of outward wholeness in those who serve at the altar. Specific defects such as blindness, lameness, or other physical impairments are explicitly listed, and those with such blemishes are forbidden to offer sacrifices or approach the holy offerings. While these restrictions bar blemished priests from active service, they are still permitted to partake of the sacred bread, highlighting both a separation in function and continued inclusion within the covenant community. This teaching underscores the importance of holiness and purity in worship, reflecting God's standards for those who minister before Him.
